newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bids seen 5.45-5.55 pct in Portugal bond auction.
newsitem.headline: Bids seen 5.45-5.55 pct in Portugal bond auction.

text.p: Most bids in today's auction of three-year fixed-rate Portuguese bonds were expected to stand at between 5.45 and 5.55 percent, but the Institute of Public Debt Management (IGCP) was not expected to place bonds above 5.50 percent, dealers said.
"Most of the demand will come out between 5.45 and 5.55 percent, but the IGCP may cut off bids at 5.50 percent," said one fixed income analyst.
Another said: "I think the auction could be fully placed (25 billion escudos), and that the average weighted interest rate could turn out around 5.45 percent."
Results of the auction are due around 1000 GMT.

Analysts said they expected strong demand from institutional investors and that the auction should benefit from expectations of good April year-on-year inflation data of between 1.7 and 2.0 percent, due to be released later this month.

At the last auction on April 8, the IGCP placed 25 billion escudos at an average weighted interest rate of 5.8959 percent, which compares with 5.48 percent at the close of the secondary market yesterday, 18 basis points above April 2000 Bonos.
